I farm by what I saw work on my own land and on other people’s land around me. I will not change too much from last year, because changing too much is risky. I have only 6 mu, so every bag of fertilizer costs money, but losing yield costs more than wasting a little fertilizer. Since I have well water, I will keep the land in two parts, 3 mu cotton and 3 mu spring maize, so the family has both cash from cotton and grain from maize. For cotton, I will use an improved seed like the people around here use, put the base fertilizer in first, then add more when it starts setting buds and bolls. Cotton can eat fertilizer for a long time, so I will not let it go hungry. I will water it about 3 times if the sky does not help, and I will spray about 4 times because aphids, mites, and boll insects can ruin it fast. For spring maize, I will use hybrid seed because that is what usually gives better ears here. I will plough or rotary till before sowing, put most of the phosphate in first, and chase nitrogen later around jointing and big bell stage. With well irrigation, I will plan on 3 waterings for maize too. If the season is smooth, I will count on maize around 650 kilos per mu and cotton around 320 kilos seed cotton per mu. That is not the highest talk people make, but it is a steady way I can afford.
